newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FREES PRICES OF 15 BASIC FOODS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FREES PRICES OF 15 BASIC FOODS.

text.p: Bulgaria on Monday further liberalised prices by lifting controls on 15 basic foods as required by the International Monetary Fund, Trade Minister Valentin Vassilev said.

"The government decided to scrap the state control on prices of flour, bread, meat, milk, cooking oil and sugar and to adopt a new mechanism of flexible prices," Vassilev told reporters. The list also includes two kinds of cheese, and sausage and eggs.
Under the new mechanism, flexible prices will be negotiated between producers and traders, Vassilev said.

The decree proposes that retailers should put stickers on the goods showing the price agreed between producers and traders. The mechanism will be in force once the cabinet decree is published in the State Gazette.

"Until wholesale markets are launched this mechanism is considered the only way to protect producers and consumers from racketeering by strong arm groups which have monopolised the market," Vassilev said.
Bulgaria is planning to launch its first wholesale markets no earlier than October. Last month the government formed a state commission to start licensing procedures. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
